name: Roche lobe overflow, two stars
blurb: Two resolved γ = 5/3 stars, neither with a point mass in it: a Sun-like star just filling its Roche lobe, and a 0.6 solar mass star of 0.6 solar radii. Both start tidally locked and settled in the Roche potential, each reaching to L1, and the larger pours gas onto the smaller. The donor is the heavier of the two, so the transfer grows. In the frame turning with the orbit, which follows the axis of the pair’s mass so that the binary stands still: in a frame turning at the starting rate the same pair swung round the grid and spiraled together within two orbits.

featured.label: Roche lobe fill
featured.tip: The donor’s radius over its Roche lobe’s (Eggleton 1983), which sets the separation: 1 just fills it, above 1 it overflows from the start. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Follow the orbit
featured.tip: The corotating frame turns faster or slower as the orbit changes, keeping the axis of the pair’s mass where it started. Off, it turns at the starting rate, and the binary swings round the grid. Changing it starts the run again
